sources.title: https://www.scandinaviastandard.com/quirky-and-unusual-places-to-visit-in-copenhagen/
sources.claim: Copenhagen offbeat spots include the Barbie Museum (4,000+ Barbies, the only such collection in Denmark, by collector Lene Darlie Pedersen), the Geological Museum's 'One Room' of oddities (taxidermied polar bear, pickled specimens), and the Glyptotek's Nasothek of 100+ severed marble noses.

sources.title: https://www.atlasobscura.com/things-to-do/stockholm-sweden/museums
sources.claim: Stockholm's unusual museums include the Spritmuseum (Museum of Spirits) and a Dala-horse museum tucked inside a souvenir shop.

sources.title: https://www.the500hiddensecrets.com/sweden/stockholm/culture/unusual-museums
sources.claim: Vrak – Museum of Wrecks (Djurgården, Stockholm) is an interactive maritime museum focused on sunken ships and Baltic underwater archaeology.

sources.title: https://www.globeguide.ca/10-quirky-fun-things-stockholm-sweden/
sources.claim: Stockholm's Toy Museum displays about 40,000 toys in a 2,500 sqm former torpedo workshop underground on Skeppsholmen.

sources.title: https://www.visitnorway.com/things-to-do/art-culture/quirky-museums/
sources.claim: Oslo's Mini Bottle Gallery is billed as the only museum of its kind in the world, with ~50,000 miniature bottles across three storeys (some containing fruit, worms or mice) plus a 'horror room'.

sources.title: https://theholidaze.com/offbeat-oslo-norway-quirky-travel-guide/
sources.claim: Oslo's Norsk Tryllemuseum (Norway Museum of Magic) shows posters, props and gear and opens only Sundays 1pm-4pm with a 2pm magic show.

sources.title: https://hotellijaravintolamuseo.fi/en/
sources.claim: Helsinki's Hotel and Restaurant Museum at the Cable Factory runs a multisensory 'Taste Matters' exhibition on Finnish culinary culture; one ticket also covers the Theatre Museum and Finnish Museum of Photography in the same complex.

sources.title: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Icelandic_Phallological_Museum
sources.claim: Reykjavik's Icelandic Phallological Museum displays over 300 penises from 100+ species (website lists 280 from 93), draws ~70,000 visitors/year, opens daily, and in December 2024 added the largest verified human penis cast (Matt Barr, 36cm).

sources.title: https://www.reykjavikcars.com/blog/activities/penis-museum
sources.claim: Icelandic Phallological Museum admission is 2750 ISK (~USD 20) with 20% off via Reykjavik City Card and free entry for children 13 and under; it has relocated to a larger harbour-side space with a phallic-themed bistro.

sources.title: https://www.dark-tourism.com/index.php/931-viru-hotel-kgb-museum-tour-tallinn
sources.claim: Tallinn's Hotel Viru KGB Museum occupies a secret 23rd-floor radio centre from which KGB agents spied on foreign guests during the Soviet era; visited by guided tour.

sources.title: https://clumsygirltravels.com/museums-in-tallinn/
sources.claim: Tallinn's Kalev Marzipan Museum at Café Maiasmokk (Estonia's oldest café) lets visitors watch marzipan figures hand-painted, while the separate Marzipan Gallery shows elaborate marzipan sculptures of city sights.

sources.title: https://www.tripadvisor.com/Attraction_Review-g274958-d2136241-Reviews-or60-KGB_Museum-Tallinn_Harju_County.html
sources.claim: Tallinn's KGB Prison Cells museum (Pagari 1) preserves the Soviet basement prison with six cells and a solitary confinement cell; admission about €10, open daily 10-18.

sources.title: https://thelasttuesdaysociety.org/museum/
sources.claim: The Viktor Wynd Museum of Curiosities (London, Hackney) is a celebration of the bizarre with two-headed lambs, mermaid skeletons, mummified fairies and an absinthe parlour; open Tue-Fri 15:00-23:00, Sat 12:00-23:00, Sun 12:00-22:00, reservations strongly encouraged, children only before 5pm.

sources.title: https://globetotting.com/weird-museums-in-london/
sources.claim: The Viktor Wynd Museum holds the gold-plated skull of a hippopotamus once owned by drug lord Pablo Escobar plus the country's largest curation of traditional absinthes.

sources.title: https://www.soane.org/your-visit
sources.claim: Sir John Soane's Museum, London, is an architect's mansion preserved as he left it ~200 years ago crammed with curiosities including the sarcophagus of pharaoh Seti I; entry is free, open Wed-Sun 10am-5pm, no pre-booking but limited space, ticketed Highlights Tours daily at midday.

sources.title: https://www.camera-obscura.co.uk/
sources.claim: Camera Obscura & World of Illusions on Edinburgh's Royal Mile is Scotland's oldest purpose-built attraction (est. 1835), with five floors and 100 interactive illusion exhibits plus a working camera obscura and rooftop views.

sources.title: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Camera_Obscura,_Edinburgh
sources.claim: Camera Obscura Edinburgh was established in 1835 as Short's Observatory and houses a working camera obscura projecting a live tour of the city onto a viewing table.

sources.title: https://museum.rcsed.ac.uk/plan-your-visit/opening-hours-and-admission
sources.claim: Surgeons' Hall Museums Edinburgh, run by the Royal College of Surgeons, are open Tue-Sat 10:00-17:00 (last admission 16:30) with a paid admission and advance booking recommended in peak season.

sources.title: https://www.atlasobscura.com/places/royal-college-surgeons-edinburgh
sources.claim: Surgeons' Hall Museums display gruesome pathology specimens, a book bound from the skin of murderer William Burke, and Burke's death mask in the Burke and Hare exhibit; ranked 8th-strangest museum in Europe.

sources.title: https://www.gla.ac.uk/hunterian/visit/
sources.claim: The Hunterian Museum, in a Gothic-revival University of Glasgow building, displays William Hunter's collection including pickled organs in jars, deformed-animal specimens and dinosaur skeletons; admission is free, open Tue-Sat 10am-5pm, pre-booking recommended.

sources.title: https://citydays.com/places/sharmanka-kinetic-theatre/
sources.claim: Sharmanka Kinetic Theatre in Glasgow, founded by Russian sculptor Eduard Bersudsky, animates 'kinemats' built from scrap metal and carved wood that lurch to light and music telling tales of Communist Russia's past.

sources.title: https://www.sharmanka.com/whats-on
sources.claim: Sharmanka Kinetic Theatre runs two ticketed shows, 'Journey' and 'Wheels of Life', each with a running time of 45 minutes, booked via TicketSource.

sources.title: https://www.littlemuseum.ie/
sources.claim: The Little Museum of Dublin at 15 St Stephen's Green is the 'people's museum', seen by 29-minute guided tour only, open 9:30am-5:00pm daily (last entry 4:30pm); advance booking recommended.

sources.title: https://www.marshlibrary.ie/
sources.claim: Marsh's Library, Dublin's first public library (1707), is open Tue-Fri 9:30-17:00 and Sat 10:00-17:00, closed Sun and bank holidays; admission EUR8 adults, EUR6 students/seniors, under-18s free.

sources.title: https://gocity.com/en/dublin/things-to-do/quirky-and-little-museums-in-dublin
sources.claim: Dublin's National Leprechaun Museum walks visitors through oversized giant furniture to feel leprechaun-sized while a guide tells Irish folklore tales; a darker 'DarkLand' evening tour is also offered.

sources.title: https://www.museedelamagie.com/
sources.claim: Paris Musée de la Magie sits in a 16th-century vaulted cellar, bundles 100+ animated automata, optical illusions and a short live magic show, and opens Wed/Sat/Sun 2-7pm (daily during zone C school holidays).

sources.title: https://www.cometoparis.com/blog/unusual-museums-paris-s1284
sources.claim: Paris Musée de la Chasse et de la Nature is housed in a Marais mansion full of high-quality taxidermy including a standing polar bear, cheetahs, tiger and baby elephant, making it a surreal hunting-and-nature detour.

sources.title: https://musee-egouts.paris.fr/en/
sources.claim: The Musée des Égouts de Paris takes visitors underground into ~500m of the operational sewer network; reopened after a major overhaul, it runs Tue-Sun 10am-5pm (last entry 4pm), closed 1 May, 25 Dec and the first half of January, €9 full / €7 reduced, free under-26 EU.

sources.title: https://www.iamsterdam.com/en/see-and-do/museums-and-galleries/unusual-museums-in-amsterdam
sources.claim: Amsterdam's Micropia (inside Artis) is the only museum in the world devoted entirely to microbes, with interactive exhibits that scan you to estimate the microbes living on your body.

sources.title: https://hollandhereicome.com/kattenkabinet-cat-museum-amsterdam/
sources.claim: Amsterdam's KattenKabinet (Cat Cabinet) is a 17th-century Herengracht canal house devoted to cats in art with works by Rembrandt, Picasso and Steinlen; a ~30-45 min visit, open Tue-Sun 12-5pm, €12.50 adults / €7.50 students / free under 12.

sources.title: https://practicalwanderlust.com/weird-museums-in-brussels/
sources.claim: Brussels' Sewer Museum (Musée des Égouts) walks visitors through a stretch of the real sewage network with an audio guide narrated by two sewer workers; open by appointment Wed-Sat 10am-5pm, from €10, free the first Sunday of each month.

sources.title: https://theculturetrip.com/europe/belgium/articles/the-10-most-unusual-museums-in-brussels
sources.claim: Brussels' Clockarium is a museum filled entirely with Art Deco ceramic mantel clocks, and the Brussels Comics Figurines Museum dedicates whole rooms to Smurfs, Tintin, Spirou plus manga and Marvel figurines.

sources.title: https://www.visitbruges.be/en/things-to-do/culture-and-heritage/lumina-domestica-lamp-museum
sources.claim: Bruges' Lumina Domestica (Lamp Museum) holds 6,000+ antique lamps tracing 400,000 years of indoor lighting from torches to LEDs, including a section on bioluminescent animals and plants.

sources.title: https://www.visitbruges.be/en/things-to-do/culture-and-heritage/frietmuseum-belgian-fries-museum
sources.claim: Bruges' Frietmuseum is the world's first and only museum dedicated to Belgian fries, set in the medieval Saaihalle with a cellar café; admission €12 adults / €10 seniors-students / €7 children 3-11, with a €0.50 fries discount.

sources.title: https://museumplantinmoretus.be/en
sources.claim: Antwerp's Museum Plantin-Moretus, a UNESCO site, is the preserved 16th-century home-and-workshop of the Plantin-Moretus printing dynasty, holding the two oldest printing presses in the world and the only surviving original Garamond letter dies; it closes for renovation 3 Aug-4 Dec 2026.

sources.title: https://slowtravelantwerp.com/en/museum-snijders-rockox/
sources.claim: Antwerp's Snijders & Rockox House merges two adjacent 17th-century patrician homes of painter Frans Snijders and collector-mayor Nicolaas Rockox, presented as a lived-in house with an iPad guide rather than a conventional gallery.

sources.title: https://travelsoffthecuff.com/ultimate-guide-to-antwerp-museums/
sources.claim: Antwerp's Red Star Line Museum, set in the line's authentic former dockside buildings, tells the story of the millions of European emigrants who sailed from Antwerp to North America in the early 20th century.

sources.title: https://www.berlin.de/en/museums/3110084-3104050-computerspielemuseum.en.html
sources.claim: Berlin's Computerspielemuseum (Karl-Marx-Allee 93A) covers gaming culture since the 1950s with 300+ exhibits and a playable retro arcade, open daily 10:00-20:00, admission EUR 12 / 8 reduced in 2026.

sources.title: https://www.ddr-museum.de/en/visit
sources.claim: Berlin's DDR Museum is an interactive East-German daily-life museum (sit in a Trabi, recreated GDR apartment, simulated Stasi surveillance), open daily 09:00-21:00, admission EUR 13.90 / 8.50 reduced.

sources.title: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deutsches_Currywurst_Museum
sources.claim: Berlin's Deutsches Currywurst Museum has been permanently closed since 21 December 2018 and is not operating in 2026 despite still appearing on many listings.

sources.title: https://www.visitberlin.de/en/museums-curiosity
sources.claim: Berlin clusters several offbeat single-theme museums including the Museum of Things (Werkbundarchiv), the DesignPanoptikum and spycraft museums alongside the Computerspielemuseum.

sources.title: https://www.bestattungsmuseum.at
sources.claim: Vienna's Funeral Museum (Bestattungsmuseum) at the Central Cemetery exhibits a reusable trapdoor coffin and 'save-yourself' bells against premature burial; open Wed-Fri 10:00-16:00, admission EUR 9.

sources.title: https://www.onb.ac.at/museen/globenmuseum
sources.claim: Vienna's Globe Museum (Palais Mollard) is the world's only public globe museum with 240 Earth, celestial, lunar and Mars globes; open Tue-Sun 10:00-18:00, EUR 6 combined ticket with the Esperanto Museum.

sources.title: https://www.onb.ac.at/museen/esperantomuseum
sources.claim: Vienna's Esperanto Museum, in the same Palais Mollard building, is one of the world's oldest language museums and documents over 500 constructed languages; Tue-Sun 10:00-18:00, EUR 6 combined ticket.

sources.title: https://www.wien.info/en/art-culture/museums-exhibitions/unusual-museums-362400
sources.claim: Vienna's deep bench of quirky museums also includes the Snow Globe Museum (Perzy family, inventors of the Viennese snow globe), the Third Man Museum (2,500 film exhibits, open Sat only) and the Clock Museum (700 working clocks).

sources.title: https://www.jagd-fischerei-museum.de/
sources.claim: Munich's Deutsches Jagd- und Fischereimuseum, in a former church on Neuhauser Strasse, is famous for displays of Wolpertingers, mythical Bavarian taxidermy-hybrid creatures; entry around EUR 5, cash only.

sources.title: https://www.atlasobscura.com/things-to-do/munich-germany
sources.claim: Munich offbeat picks include the Valentin-Karlstadt-Musaeum (comedy museum in the Isartor tower honoring Karl Valentin), the Munich Toy Museum (four floors in the Old Town Hall tower) and the city's potato museum.

sources.title: https://www.uzh.ch/en/explore/museums/moulagenmuseum.html
sources.claim: Zurich's Moulagenmuseum at the University of Zurich holds one of the world's largest collections of lifelike wax casts of skin diseases and injuries (leprous noses, eye ulcers, ear abscesses).

sources.title: https://www.swissinfo.ch/eng/culture/from-the-cute-to-the-horrific-switzerlands-weirdest-museums/77796301
sources.claim: Switzerland's weirdest museums include Zurich's Wax Moulage museum, Basel's Spielzeug Welten Museum (2,500 teddy bears, world's largest such collection) and the Henkermuseum hangman/torture museum in Sissach near Basel.

sources.title: https://www.tinguely.ch/en/information/admission.html
sources.claim: Basel's Museum Tinguely houses the world's largest collection of Jean Tinguely's kinetic sculptures that whirr and move at the push of a button; open Tue-Sun 11:00-18:00 (Thu to 21:00), closed Mondays.

sources.title: https://www.miniatur-wunderland.com/visiting/extras/hamburg/
sources.claim: Hamburg's Miniatur Wunderland in the Speicherstadt is the world's largest model railway with 1,100+ trains, 289,000 figures and a working miniature airport, peppered with thousands of hidden humorous scenes.

sources.title: https://www.hamburg-travel.com/see-explore/culture-music/museums-galleries/spicys-gewuerzmuseum/
sources.claim: Hamburg's Spicy's Gewuerzmuseum in the Speicherstadt is a smell-touch-taste spice museum with 900+ exhibits across five centuries and free entry, making a quick offbeat half-hour stop.

sources.title: https://tourter.com/czech-republic/prague/unusual-museums-in-prague
sources.claim: Prague's Sex Machines Museum is the world's only museum dedicated to mechanical erotic devices, ~200 items, roughly a 1-hour visit near Old Town Square; the Speculum Alchemiae offers half-hourly English guided tours of a real 16th-century alchemy lab with hidden tunnels; and the Museum of Historical Chamber Pots and Toilets holds over 2,000 items.

sources.title: https://www.tripadvisor.com/Attraction_Review-g274707-d609902-Reviews-Sex_Machines_Museum-Prague_Bohemia.html
sources.claim: Prague's Sex Machines Museum is a specialty museum near Old Town Square taking about an hour, with a small cinema showing vintage erotic films.

sources.title: https://flippermuzeum.hu/en/contact-prices/
sources.claim: Budapest's Pinball Museum (Flippermúzeum) at Radnóti Miklós utca 18 deploys 160+ machines set to free play, opens Wed-Sun (closed Mon/Tue), admission HUF 5,500 (HUF 4,000 discount); 1-2 hour interactive visit.

sources.title: https://www.sziklakorhaz.eu/en/prices
sources.claim: Budapest's Hospital in the Rock (Sziklakórház) — a WWII emergency hospital and Cold War nuclear bunker under Buda Castle — is visitable only via a 60-minute guided tour departing hourly, daily 10:00-19:00, adult ticket HUF 5,800.

sources.title: https://www.tripadvisor.com/Attraction_Review-g274887-d10475152-Reviews-The_House_of_Houdini-Budapest_Central_Hungary.html
sources.claim: Budapest's House of Houdini is a museum dedicated to the Hungarian-born illusionist, displaying original props, handcuffs, letters and movie props, capped with a 15-minute live magic performance.

sources.title: https://www.tripadvisor.com/Attraction_Review-g294454-d1929841-Reviews-Museum_of_Broken_Relationships-Zagreb_Central_Croatia.html
sources.claim: Zagreb's Museum of Broken Relationships displays donated mementos of failed relationships from around the world, each paired with its breakup story; admission around 7 EUR (5.50 EUR concessions).

sources.title: https://whichmuseum.com/museum/museum-of-illusions-zagreb-7722/tickets-prices
sources.claim: Zagreb's Museum of Illusions invites visitors to interact with mind-bending optical displays and become the exhibits, a quick 1-hour quirky stop.

sources.title: https://www.tripadvisor.com/Attraction_Review-g274772-d9769262-Reviews-Krakow_Pinball_Museum-Krakow_Lesser_Poland_Province_Southern_Poland.html
sources.claim: Krakow Pinball Museum holds 80+ pinball/arcade machines from the 1950s onward across ~300m2 in a 15th-century cellar, with unlimited free play included in the ticket.

sources.title: https://www.tripadvisor.com/Attraction_Review-g274772-d3194318-Reviews-Eagle_Pharmacy_Museum_of_Krakow-Krakow_Lesser_Poland_Province_Southern_Poland.html
sources.claim: Krakow's Pharmacy Under the Eagle (Apteka Pod Orłem) in Podgórze was the only pharmacy in the Krakow ghetto, now a small evocative Holocaust exhibit with three historic films — a sobering ~1-hour visit.

sources.title: https://krakowbooking.com/blog/unusual-museums-krakow
sources.claim: Krakow's offbeat museum scene also includes the LEGO-based Bricks & Figs Museum with massive dioramas and pop-culture figures, plus vodka, bagel and illusion-themed spots.

sources.title: https://www.mywanderlust.pl/the-wonderful-unusual-neon-museum-in-warsaw/
sources.claim: Warsaw's Neon Museum in the Praga district preserves Cold War-era neon signs (~50 neons, nearly 500 letters) at the Soho Factory, a quirky ~1-hour off-the-beaten-path stop with a low entry fee.

sources.title: https://muzea.waw.pl/en/guides/unusual-museums-warsaw/
sources.claim: Warsaw's Polish Vodka Museum sits in a heritage rectification plant that produced spirits from 1897, with five interactive galleries and a guided tasting (3-4 vodkas) included; a self-blend nalewka station adds a hands-on twist.

sources.title: https://www.culturaobscura.com/recharging-at-pinball-station-in-warsaw/
sources.claim: Warsaw's Pinball Station, founded 2016 by two collectors, now holds 100+ machines (60 restored and playable); a 40 PLN wristband gives all-day unlimited play with re-entry until closing.

sources.title: https://museumspotlighteurope.com/a-peculiar-journey-into-the-puppet-museum-of-ljubljana/
sources.claim: Ljubljana's Museum of Puppetry, housed inside Ljubljana Castle, greets visitors with decapitated puppet heads and interactive exhibits and can be combined with a castle visit.

sources.title: https://houseofillusions.si/en/
sources.claim: Ljubljana's House of Illusions on Kongresni trg offers 70+ interactive exhibits including an Anti-Gravity Room and an Infinity Disco Room — a fun ~1-hour central stop.

sources.title: https://visitbucharest.today/grigore-antipa-national-museum/
sources.claim: Bucharest's Grigore Antipa Natural History Museum is packed with lifelike dioramas, fossils and a recreated 11m-long cave with stalactites, fossils and bat colonies plus a Deinotherium giant elephant skeleton — a strong half-day family stop.

sources.title: https://www.atlasobscura.com/places/the-romanian-kitsch-museum-bucharest-romania
sources.claim: Bucharest's Romanian Kitsch Museum (opened May 2017, Old Town) divided tacky exhibits into Dracula, religious, communist and gypsy kitsch sections with a make-your-own-kitsch corner, but multiple on-the-ground reports describe it as closed indefinitely / replaced by a bar, so its 2026 status is uncertain.

sources.title: https://kitschmuseum.ro/
sources.claim: The Romanian Kitsch Museum's own website is outdated and even carries a 'kind of closed' notice, listing prior admission of 20 RON / 4 EUR and directing visitors to phone/email to confirm — reinforcing that 2026 visitors should verify before going.

sources.title: https://www.tripadvisor.com/Attraction_Review-g187791-d254786-Reviews-Museum_and_Crypt_of_Capuchins_Friars-Rome_Lazio.html
sources.claim: Rome's Capuchin Crypt beneath Santa Maria della Concezione is decorated with the bones of over 4,000 friars across themed rooms (skulls, pelvises, leg bones) and is open 9am-7pm, rarely crowded.

sources.title: https://www.islands.com/1683780/museum-holy-souls-purgatory-creepy-museum-rome-italy-unsettling/
sources.claim: Rome's tiny Museum of the Holy Souls in Purgatory (inside Chiesa del Sacro Cuore del Suffragio, Prati) displays scorched handprints said to be left by souls in purgatory; no website, contact the church for hours, modest dress required.

sources.title: https://www.museosansevero.it/en/plan-your-visit/opening-hours-fees
sources.claim: Naples' Sansevero Chapel Museum (home of the Veiled Christ and the anatomical machines) is open daily 9am-7pm except Tuesdays, costs EUR12, and requires advance timed booking.

sources.title: https://www.visititaly.eu/places-and-tours/cimitero-delle-fontanelle-naples-opens-again
sources.claim: Naples' Fontanelle Cemetery, an ossuary cave tied to a Neapolitan cult of caring for and naming anonymous skulls, reopened 18 April 2026 after restoration; now open daily 10am-6pm except Wednesdays, EUR6-8 with reservation required.

sources.title: https://www.museos.com/en/barcelona/erotic-museum-barcelona/
sources.claim: Barcelona's Erotic Museum (Museu de l'Erotica) on La Rambla, opened 1997, mixes humour, history and art across civilisations and is a popular offbeat half-day stop.

sources.title: https://www.barcelona.cat/museufredericmares/en/activitats/tothom
sources.claim: Barcelona's Museu Frederic Marès, in the Gothic Quarter's former Royal Palace, holds a Collector's Cabinet of tens of thousands of obsessively hoarded objects (fans, pipes, keys, scissors); free Sundays after 3pm and first Sunday of the month.

sources.title: https://www.esmadrid.com/en/tourist-information/cerralbo-museum
sources.claim: Madrid's Cerralbo Museum is a preserved 19th-century aristocratic house-museum with over 50,000 objects (armour, weapons, clocks, tapestries) frozen as the marquis left it.

sources.title: https://www.esmadrid.com/en/house-museums
sources.claim: Madrid's Sorolla Museum, a preserved artist house-museum with a self-designed garden, is temporarily closed for renovation and expected to reopen during 2026; the 'Another Madrid' pass (EUR12, 10 days) covers Cerralbo, Romanticism, Decorative Arts, Sorolla and Lazaro Galdiano.

sources.title: https://www.esmadrid.com/en/tourist-information/sorolla-museum
sources.claim: Madrid's Museum of Romanticism recreates the daily life and material culture of Spain's Romantic era (1833-1868) in a 19th-century mansion.

sources.title: https://www.visitlisboa.com/en/places/national-tile-museum
sources.claim: Lisbon's Museu Nacional do Azulejo, the only tile museum of its kind in the world, traces 500 years of Portuguese azulejo in the former Madre de Deus Convent, including a 23-metre panorama of pre-1755 Lisbon.

sources.title: https://neighbourlylisbon.com/see/lisbon-museums/museu-azulejo-portuguese-tiles-museum/
sources.claim: Lisbon's Azulejo (Tile) Museum is closed for renovations with only the shop accessible, expected to reopen mid-2026.

sources.title: https://airial.travel/attractions/portugal/lisboa/aljube-museum-resistance-and-freedom-lisbon-9kTQquOn
sources.claim: Lisbon's Aljube Museum - Resistance and Freedom occupies a former dictatorship-era political prison next to the Se Cathedral and documents resistance against the Salazar regime.

sources.title: https://www.atlasobscura.com/places/museum-of-greek-folk-musical-instruments
sources.claim: Athens' Museum of Greek Folk Musical Instruments in Plaka displays 1,200+ traditional instruments and shadow puppets over three floors with listening headphones, gathered over 50 years by musicologist Fivos Anoyanakis; rarely crowded, ~1 hour.

sources.title: https://www.magicum.berlin/en/
sources.claim: Magicum — the Berlin Magic Museum — is an interactive museum of magic set in cellar vaults, exploring magical practices across cultures (African voodoo, shamanic rituals, astrology, alchemy); open daily 11:00-18:00.
